The title of the left table is X, listing x=0,1,2,3, with corresponding probabilities respectively 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1. Reasoning: Z=X+Y, and it asks for P(Z≤2), which is to enumerate all combinations satisfying x+y≤2. Because the minimum value of Y is 1, the feasible combinations are (0,1), (1,1), (0,2). X and Y are independent, so the joint probability equals the product of marginal probabilities: P(0,1)=0.4×0.1=0.04, P(1,1)=0.3×0.1=0.03, P(0,2)=0.4×0.2=0.08. Adding them gives 0.04+0.03+0.08=0.15.

raw_record.question_text: X and Y are independent random variables; the probability distributions for each are given in the table above. Let Z = X + Y. What is P(Z ≤ 2)?

method.method_draft: Read the image as two side-by-side probability tables: for X, values 0, 1, 2, 3 have probabilities 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1; for Y, values 1, 2, 3, 4 have probabilities 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4. From the text, use Z = X + Y and the target P(Z ≤ 2). Enumerate all value pairs with x + y ≤ 2: (0,1), (1,1), and (0,2). Since X and Y are independent, multiply probabilities for each pair and add: P(0,1)=0.4·0.1, P(1,1)=0.3·0.1, P(0,2)=0.4·0.2. Sum these products to get 0.15.

method.method_draft: Read the image tables to obtain P(Y=1)=0.1, P(Y=2)=0.2, and the needed cumulative probabilities for X: P(X≤1)=0.4+0.3=0.7 and P(X≤0)=0.4. From the text, use Z=X+Y and compute P(X+Y≤2) by conditioning on Y. Since Y can be 1, 2, 3, or 4, only Y=1 and Y=2 can contribute: if Y=1, need X≤1; if Y=2, need X≤0; if Y≥3, no nonnegative X value in the table can make the sum ≤2. Therefore P(Z≤2)=P(Y=1)P(X≤1)+P(Y=2)P(X≤0)=0.1·0.7+0.2·0.4=0.15.
